text: Finally watched Dune (2021) and I get the hype. The sound design alone deserves an award. Timothée as Paul Atreides was great. Part Two tonight!
just watched oppenheimer and i have so many thoughts. the trinity test sequence in dead silence?? incredible.
Oppenheimer's runtime is three hours and I never once checked my phone. Cillian Murphy deserved every award. No spoilers but the black-and-white scenes with Robert Downey Jr. are the best part.
Barbie was so much funnier than I expected. Ryan Gosling's "I'm just Ken" number lived rent-free in my head for a week. 💗
Went to see the Barbie movie in a pink outfit with my mum and we both cried at the Ruth Handler scene. Greta Gerwig did something special.
The Joker staircase dance is one of the best movie scenes of the decade. Joaquin Phoenix was terrifying. Not for everyone but a masterpiece to me.
Rewatched Titanic last night. Still crying. And yes, there was room on the door. Fight me.
titanic still holds up after 25 years. The practical sets, Kate Winslet, that sinking sequence. Cameron really did that.
Rewatching Avatar before the new one and honestly the visuals still look insane for a film from 2009. Pandora is gorgeous. Jake Sully's whole arc works.
Her is the loneliest and most beautiful movie ever made. Theodore Twombly and his operating system broke me. Watched it again last night and cried at the same scene.
Jordan Peele's Us is such a tight, weird horror movie. The doppelganger scenes with the scissors are going to haunt me. Lupita Nyong'o is incredible.
Rewatched It (2017) with friends and the Pennywise clown scenes still freak me out. Bill Skarsgård is nightmare fuel. Floating the balloon in the sewer. Nope. 🎈
Alien (1979) is the perfect horror movie. Ripley, the chestburster, the claustrophobia, the cat. Ridley Scott knew exactly what he was doing.
Jaws is still the best summer blockbuster ever made. "You're gonna need a bigger boat" and that opening scene. Spielberg was in his 20s!!
Gravity in IMAX was the most anxious 90 minutes of my life. Sandra Bullock floating around in space with zero margin for error. Never again. Absolutely again.
Inception is still my favourite Nolan film. The spinning top ending. The folded city. The Hans Zimmer BRAAAM. Watch it again and tell me it isn't perfect.
did the top fall or not, i need to know. i've watched inception 14 times and i'm still not sure
Austin Butler as Elvis was a revelation. The Baz Luhrmann style is too much for some people but I'd happily watch it again just for the Vegas sequence.

Napoleon (2023) is a weird film. Joaquin Phoenix plays him like a sulky teenager, the battle of Austerlitz is amazing, and the tone is nonstop dark comedy. Not what I expected. Ridley Scott did his thing.
Watched Gandhi (1982) for a history class and Ben Kingsley is mesmerising in it. Three hours long but I'd watch the salt march scene again.
Daniel Day-Lewis in Lincoln is just frightening good. The whole movie is two guys in a room negotiating a vote and I was on the edge of my seat.
Venom is bad and I love it. Tom Hardy arguing with a symbiote in a lobster tank is peak 2018 cinema. "Turd in the wind" will never be topped.
Running up those Philadelphia museum steps is basically a rite of passage now. Rocky is a better drama than a boxing film. Stallone wrote it in three days!
Selena (1997) with Jennifer Lopez still gets me every time. The Astrodome concert scene is so emotional. #Selena
Will Smith as Muhammad Ali in Ali is a really underrated performance. Michael Mann's film has a few slow spots but the training montages are great.
Home (2015) is a cute kid's film and I will not take criticism. Oh and Rihanna's songs slap.
Cars is Pixar's most underrated film, and I'll defend it forever. Lightning McQueen's arc, Doc Hudson, that Route 66 nostalgia. Ka-chow! 🏎️
The first ten minutes of Up are the most devastating thing Pixar ever made. Carl and Ellie. I'm not okay. Then the rest of the movie is a delightful adventure.
Inside Out is a perfect movie about growing up. Riley's emotions are exactly how my head feels. Bing Bong's goodbye scene destroys me every time.
The Dark Knight turned 15 and Heath Ledger's Joker is still the standard. The interrogation scene is a masterclass.
The Matrix is still a masterpiece. Bullet-time, the lobby scene, the philosophical stuff that went over my head at 14 and still does. "There is no spoon."
No Way Home is such a love letter to every Spider-Man fan. When the three Peters were on screen together I lost it. No spoilers but wow. 🕷️
Interstellar's docking scene with the Hans Zimmer organ is peak cinema. I will never recover from the Murph reunion. And the bookshelf scene. Cooper, why.
Parasite deserved Best Picture. The flood scene, the stairs motif, the peach allergy. Bong Joon-ho is a genius.
Top Gun: Maverick is the best sequel in years. The flight sequences are real. Tom Cruise on the stick, no CGI. I walked out of the theatre needing a cigarette. And I don't smoke.
Get Out's "sunken place" scene is one of the best horror moments ever. Jordan Peele made a great film about race and I'm still thinking about it.
The Shawshank Redemption is on TV again and I'll be watching it for the 30th time. "Get busy living or get busy dying." Andy Dufresne is my hero.
Frozen's "Let It Go" scene still gives me goosebumps. My niece has watched it 200 times. I know every lyric whether I like it or not.
Finding Nemo made me cry in the first five minutes. Dory is the funniest character. "Just keep swimming" is life advice. 🐠
Coco is a gorgeous film about family and memory. "Remember Me" at the end. I sobbed ugly in front of my kids. Highly recommend.
Encanto's "We Don't Talk About Bruno" was stuck in my head for six months. The film itself is lovely too, especially Mirabel and Isabela. Don't @ me.
WALL-E is the best sci-fi romance ever made, and most of it has no dialogue. Just a little robot and his cockroach. Pixar was cooking.
Ratatouille is a masterpiece about art and critics. Anton Ego's review speech gets me every time. "Anyone can cook." 🐀
Mulan is a better soldier than half the guys in my unit. "Reflection" is a song I still sing on dark days. Disney classics hit different.
"Are you not entertained?" Gladiator is the ultimate revenge film. Russell Crowe as Maximus, the wheat field, the Hans Zimmer score. Perfection.
John Wick is what happens when you kill a man's dog. The Continental, the gold coins, the gun-fu choreography. I've watched all four. Baba Yaga.
Black Panther changed things. Wakanda Forever. Chadwick Boseman was so good. The Killmonger scene still hurts. Rest in power.
Don't Look Up is a bit on the nose, but it made me laugh and then made me feel terrible. Leo and Jennifer Lawrence were both fantastic. Meryl is scary good.
Whiplash gave me so much anxiety I forgot to eat my popcorn. "Not my tempo!" J.K. Simmons is terrifying. The final drum solo is perfection.
Ghostbusters is a perfect summer movie. Slimer, the Stay Puft Marshmallow Man, "Who ya gonna call?". Bill Murray is a legend.
Home Alone on Christmas Eve is a tradition in my house. Kevin McCallister's booby traps are still hilarious. "Keep the change, ya filthy animal."
Shrek is somehow both a fairy tale parody and a genuinely great romance. "All Star" at the start, Lord Farquaad, Donkey. 2001 had it all.
Despicable Me is a really sweet movie. The three little girls, Gru's heart growing three sizes. And the Minions, obviously. Banana!
The Lord of the Rings is the only book I've read more than five times. Every reread I find something new, like the song of Tom Bombadil. LotR is life.
Finally finished Dune the novel and wow. The ecology, the politics, the Bene Gesserit. Frank Herbert built a whole world. Now onto Dune Messiah. Don't spoil it for me.
Animal Farm in a class discussion today: "All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others." My students got it immediately. Smart kids. Orwell is always relevant.
Pride and Prejudice is still the best romance novel ever. Darcy's first proposal is a masterclass in how not to do it. Elizabeth Bennet is my role model.
Dracula is told through letters and diary entries and that's why it works. Jonathan Harker in the castle is pure gothic dread. Read it in October, with candles.
The Great Gatsby is a short book that deserves far more than a school reading. The green light, Daisy's voice, Gatsby's parties. "So we beat on, boats against the current."

Starting A Game of Thrones again on audiobook. I forgot how slow and careful the first chapters are. The Ned Stark chapters are a gut punch when you know what's coming. No spoilers in the replies please!
Reading Fahrenheit 451 and the part about the parlour walls full of screens feels scarily current. Bradbury saw it coming.
The Catcher in the Rye is a book you either read at 16 and love or at 30 and want to shake Holden. I think both reactions are valid. 🦆
The Alchemist is a book people either love or roll their eyes at. I read it at 19 and it sent me travelling. It's a short, hopeful fable, and sometimes that's what you need.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy is still the funniest sci-fi book I've read. Don't panic. Bring a towel. 42. Douglas Adams was a genius.
expect: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

text: Slaughterhouse-Five: "So it goes." Billy Pilgrim coming unstuck in time. Vonnegut writing about Dresden is something else. A must-read for anyone who loves weird war novels.
Jane Eyre is the original gothic romance. Thornfield Hall, the madwoman in the attic, "Reader, I married him." I've read it every year since uni.
The Silmarillion is a very different read from The Lord of the Rings. It reads like mythology. Fëanor's oath, Beren and Lúthien, the fall of Gondolin. Tolkien's best writing is hidden in here.
Reread Twilight as an adult and honestly the first third is a vibe. The Forks setting, Edward staring, the biology class. Not a great book, but a great time capsule. 🧛
Gone with the Wind is a complicated book. It's a sweeping romance with a deeply problematic view of the Civil War. I'm glad I read it, but I'd choose my words carefully when I recommend it.
Eragon was my gateway to fantasy. I was 12 and obsessed with dragons. Saphira, the Ra'zac, Arya. I can't judge it now, it's too tied up with my childhood.
Of Mice and Men is 100 pages and every sentence counts. George and Lennie, the rabbits, the dream of a farm. I cried on the bus. Steinbeck, you absolute legend.
I finally finished Moby-Dick and I regret nothing. The whaling chapters are weird and the cetology is an acquired taste, but Ahab is magnificent. "Call me Ishmael." Never forget it.

Chernobyl on HBO is the best TV miniseries I've ever seen. Jared Harris as Legasov in the courtroom. The bridge of death scene. It's heavy but you have to watch it. Five episodes and I couldn't look away.
just finished chernobyl the series and now i'm reading about the real disaster. Craig Mazin did such a good job. "What is the cost of lies?" is going to stay with me for a long time.
Lost's finale still divides people and I'll never stop defending it. The characters mattered more than the mystery. Jack, Kate, Sawyer, Hurley. Namaste. Watch it all again with me?
The first season of Lost is perfect TV. The pilot plane crash, the polar bear, the hatch. J.J. Abrams was a madman. Is anyone else rewatching it in 2025?
Friends is the show I put on when I'm sad. Rachel and Ross, Chandler's jokes, Phoebe's songs. "Smelly Cat" is a masterpiece. The One with the Embryos is peak.
Rachel Green's season 3 hair, Phoebe Buffay's "Regina Phalange" alias, Chandler Bing sarcasm. Friends is a comfort show forever. We were on a break!
Arcane is the best animated series ever made. Jinx's breakdown in episode 8? Powder? The whole thing is a masterpiece. Fortiche, please never stop. #Arcane
Severance is the most original TV show in years. The Lumon elevator, the goat room, Mr. Milchick. Season 2's finale destroyed me. Waffle party, anyone?
Succession's final season was bleak and brilliant. "I love you, but you are not serious people." Logan Roy's funeral episode is some of the best writing on TV. No spoilers, please.
Shōgun on FX is a masterclass in production. The subtitles, the politics, the Lord Toranaga's patience. Anna Sawai was incredible. Episode 5, the earthquake, I couldn't breathe.
Fallout the TV show is shockingly good. Lucy's wide-eyed vault-dweller act and The Ghoul's cynicism work so well together. The Vault-Tec stuff is hilarious. They nailed the tone of the games.
Halo on Paramount+ had its moments but the show kept being weird about Master Chief taking his helmet off. Pablo Schreiber looked the part, though. Season 2 was better than the first.
Vikings starts as a gritty drama about Ragnar Lothbrok, then turns into a bit of a soap opera. But those early seasons are fantastic. The raid on Lindisfarne in season 1 is great TV.
Wednesday Addams dancing in the school gym is the best TV scene of the year. Jenna Ortega made that role her own. Netflix, give us season 3. 🖤
Dark is the only show that made me draw a family tree on a whiteboard. Winden, the cave, the time loops. Three seasons, zero filler. German TV is underrated.
The Mandalorian season 1 had a simple formula and it worked. Mando, Grogu, the Ron Swanson-style bounty hunter. Baby Yoda was the real star. "This is the way."
Ted Lasso is a show about kindness and it's perfect. "Be a goldfish." Rebecca and Keeley, Roy Kent. Season 1 is perfection. AFC Richmond forever. ⚽
The Bear season 2's "Fishes" episode is the most stressful 70 minutes of TV I've ever watched. Chef, behind! Jeremy Allen White gives it everything.
Sherlock's "The Reichenbach Fall" is the best episode of television the BBC ever made. Moriarty's grin. Benedict Cumberbatch and Martin Freeman at their best. Elementary, my dear Watson.
The Succession episode where Kendall drops the keys and Shiv has to take the wheel. Wow. Season 4's writing is razor sharp. No wonder this show won all the awards.
Fleabag season 2 ended and I haven't recovered. The hot priest. The fourth wall. "It will pass." Phoebe Waller-Bridge, you genius.
Invincible is the best superhero show right now. Omni-Man's fight with Mark in season 1's finale is brutal. The animation's gorgeous. Please don't spoil season 3 for me.
Andor is the best Star Wars thing since the original trilogy. Luthen Rael's monologue, the prison break, "I burn my life to make a sunrise". Hats off to Tony Gilroy.
Bridgerton season 3 is giving Colin and Penelope the love story they deserve. Lady Whistledown's reveal, the ballroom scene in the rain. I'm a mess. Pass the tissues.
Hazbin Hotel is a chaotic, loud, musical about demons, and I'm hooked. Alastor's the real star. "Stayed Gone" is my current favourite song. I'm sorry to everyone I annoyed.
Love, Death & Robots is the best anthology in years. Some episodes are 6 minutes long and still hit harder than most feature films. "Zima Blue" is my favourite.
Cobra Kai is a guilty pleasure that gets better every season. Johnny Lawrence is the hero we didn't know we needed. "Strike first, strike hard, no mercy." Sweep the leg!
The Umbrella Academy season 1's opening dance scene to "I Think We're Alone Now" is perfect. Klaus is a treasure. The ending of season 4 was a letdown, though.
Seinfeld is a show about nothing and it's the best sitcom ever. The Soup Nazi, the puffy shirt, the Festivus pole. "Yada yada yada." No hugging, no learning.
Yellowstone's Beth Dutton is the best antihero in years. John Dutton's ranch, Rip Wheeler's loyalty, the family drama. The Paramount spin-offs are less good. #Yellowstone
Ozark season 4 was a masterclass in dread. Wendy Byrde's slow turn, Ruth Langmore's heartbreak. The ending was perfect, no notes.
Dexter season 4 with John Lithgow as the Trinity Killer is peak television. Don't even talk to me about the finale of season 8. Absolute mess. But the early seasons? Chef's kiss.
Euphoria is beautifully shot and horribly depressing. Zendaya as Rue deserved the Emmy. The Fezco episode in season 2 is one of the best of the decade.
The Expanse is the best sci-fi show of the last decade and people don't talk about it enough. Amos Burton, Chrisjen Avasarala, the Rocinante. Gorgeous space opera.
Alice in Borderland is a gripping survival show. The Tokyo games, Arisu and Usagi. I watched six episodes in a day and my sleep suffered.
The Penguin is Colin Farrell's showcase. I forgot it was Colin Farrell for a whole episode. Gritty Gotham crime TV at its best. Sofia Falcone's arc was a treat.
Agatha All Along is a delight. "The Ballad of the Witches' Road" has been looping in my head. Kathryn Hahn is a gift. Rio Vidal's reveal was a good twist. No more spoilers please.
Mindhunter got cancelled after two seasons and it's a crime. The Ed Kemper scenes, Holden's unravelling, the Fincher style. Netflix, bring it back!
Peacemaker has the best opening credits dance in TV. James Gunn's humour, John Cena's goofy charm, Eagly. I love this stupid, sweet show.
Rome (the HBO series) is the best historical drama ever made. Titus Pullo and Lucius Vorenus are a perfect duo. Cleopatra's introduction. Caesar's assassination. It was cancelled too soon.
Fargo season 2 is peak Coen-brothers-style TV. Kirsten Dunst, Jesse Plemons, Patrick Wilson. The UFO scene still makes me laugh. Mmm-hmm.
Monk is a perfect comfort show: a detective with OCD solving murders. Adrian Monk's "Here's what happened" bit is a delight. Tony Shalhoub was perfect.
Arrow season 2 is some of the best superhero TV ever. Slade Wilson vs. Oliver, the flashbacks to Lian Yu. The show lost its way later, but those early seasons slap.
Castlevania on Netflix is a gory, gorgeous animated vampire show. Trevor Belmont, Sypha, and Alucard are a great trio. Written by Warren Ellis. Season 3's last episode broke me.
Tears of the Kingdom's Ultrahand lets people build the wildest contraptions. I made a flying machine that drops bombs and a motorised cart that carries a cow. Nintendo gave us a sandbox.
expect: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

text: RDR2 broke me. Arthur Morgan's last ride on the mountain, I put down the controller and stared at the wall for ten minutes. Rockstar writes the best characters. No spoilers please.
New Vegas is better than any Fallout since. The Mojave Wasteland, the factions, Mr. House. "The House always wins." Obsidian wrote an RPG with real consequences.
Bloodborne is the best game FromSoftware has ever made and I don't want to hear arguments. Gothic Victorian horror, the Hunter's Dream, Father Gascoigne. Sony, please remaster it.
Sekiro is the most satisfying combat I've ever mastered. Deflecting Genichiro's attacks perfectly is pure rhythm. Shadows die twice, but I die forty times per boss.
BG3 is a game that rewards every choice. I romanced Astarion, then spent three hours on the Withers dialogue. Larian is a gift. This is how you make an RPG.
Horizon Zero Dawn's first Thunderjaw fight made me yell at my TV. Aloy's story is surprisingly deep. The robot-dinosaur world is a visual treat.
Persona 5 is stylish in every menu. "Take Your Time" is the best JRPG song ever. The Phantom Thieves, Joker, Morgana. I'm still not over the ending.
Terraria is 15 years old and it keeps getting better. I thought I knew everything, then I found the Moon Lord. A 2D sandbox with endless depth.
Valorant ranked is a different kind of stress. Jett operators, Sage heals, Sova darts. Someone on my team always rages in voice chat. Immortal soon, hopefully.
Celeste is a game about climbing a mountain and anxiety. Madeline's journey is so moving. The B-sides are hard but fair. "Resurrections" is a banger of a soundtrack. 🍓
Silksong is finally out and Hornet is a delight. The movement is so much faster than Hollow Knight. I died to the first boss 20 times and loved every attempt. Team Cherry cooked.
Hades is the best roguelike ever. Every death is a story, every run is different. Zagreus, Megaera, Thanatos. Supergiant makes games like nobody else. Dying has never felt this good.
Cuphead's boss fights are a work of art. The 1930s animation, the jazz soundtrack, the pain. Delicious Last Course was a worthy DLC. I can't believe I finished it.
Undertale is a game that makes you feel guilty for killing. Sans, Papyrus, Toriel. The Genocide route is chilling. Toby Fox made magic. You're filled with determination.
Disco Elysium has the best writing in any game I've played. Harry Du Bois's internal monologue, the Skills arguing in his head. It's a murder mystery wrapped in political philosophy.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has the best turn-based combat in ages. The parry system, the Belle Époque setting, the music. French studio Sandfall made something unforgettable. I need more time to recover.
Black Myth: Wukong's bosses are visually jaw-dropping. The Journey to the West story is amazing, and the staff combat is crisp. Game Science did something special. Destined one, climb on.
Starfield is a game with a wide ocean and a puddle's depth. Pretty planets, big ship builder, boring planetary exploration. I love Bethesda, but this was meh. Maybe the mods will fix it.
Death Stranding is the only game where carrying packages is peaceful. Hideo Kojima made a hiking sim and I'm in love. Sam Bridges, the BTs, Mads Mikkelsen. Strand type game for life.
Final Fantasy VII is the game that made me love JRPGs. Cloud, Tifa, Aerith. Her death still hits. FF7 Remake's reimagining is bold. I'll wait for part 3 with bated breath.
Animal Crossing: New Horizons got me through the lockdown. Tom Nook's loans, Isabelle's announcements, K.K. Slider on Saturdays. I still log in every day to water my flowers.
Portal is a perfect game. Two hours long, no wasted time. GLaDOS, the Companion Cube, "The cake is a lie." Valve, we need Portal 3. Still waiting.
Half-Life: Alyx is the reason to own a VR headset. The Jeff chapter had me screaming. Reloading with my real hands, sliding the shotgun. Valve, we're ready.
Doom Eternal's combat is a glory-kill ballet. Chainsaw, flame belch, blood punch, ammo. The Slayer's meat-gravy rock soundtrack by Mick Gordon is mighty. Rip and tear.
BioShock's "Would you kindly?" twist is the best in the history of gaming. Andrew Ryan, Rapture, Big Daddies. A masterpiece of environmental storytelling. And no spoilers!
My 11-year-old plays Fortnite for six hours a day and I've gone from banning it to actually playing it. I got a Victory Royale last night and screamed like a child. We're teammates now.
Roblox is huge in my daughter's school. All the kids talk about Adopt Me and Brookhaven. I looked into it, and it's mostly safe if you check the settings, but you have to be vigilant about chat.
Tetris is the only game I'll never put down. The Korobeiniki theme, the T-spin, the endless blocks. 40 years and it still hooks you. Marathon mode at 2am. 🧱
Pac-Man is the original cultural game icon. Waka waka, the four ghosts, Inky, Pinky, Blinky and Clyde. A perfect score of 3,333,360 is the stuff of legend.
Spirited Away is the best animated film I've ever seen. No-Face, Haku, the bathhouse, the train over the water. Miyazaki is a master. I watch it every time I'm homesick.
Your Name made me ugly cry on the train. The comet scene, the red thread, "Sparkle" by RADWIMPS. Makoto Shinkai painted every frame. I watched it three times in a week.
Princess Mononoke is an ecological epic with real moral complexity. Lady Eboshi is neither hero nor villain. Ashitaka's quiet determination. The forest spirit scene is stunning.
My Neighbor Totoro is the warmest film ever made. Satsuki and Mei, the Catbus, the rainy bus stop. No villains. It's pure comfort. I'm going to watch it tonight, again.
Evangelion is a show about depression disguised as a mecha anime. Shinji, get in the robot! Rei, Asuka, the end of Evangelion. I'm not sure I understood it, but it changed my life.
Cowboy Bebop is perfect from episode 1. "See you, space cowboy." Spike Spiegel, Faye Valentine, Ed. The jazz soundtrack by Yoko Kanno is something else. The best anime of all time? Probably.
Dragon Ball Z's Goku vs. Frieza fight took five episodes of charging up and I'd do it all again. Kamehameha! Super Saiyan transformation is peak childhood TV. DBZ forever.
Howl's Moving Castle is a love story about aging and being brave. Sophie's curse, Calcifer, the moving castle itself. Joe Hisaishi's waltz makes me cry. Ghibli, you've got my heart.
Akira is still the benchmark for animation in 1988. Neo-Tokyo, Kaneda's motorcycle slide, Tetsuo's transformation. The handmade backgrounds are unreal. It deserves its legend.
Ghost in the Shell (1995) is a masterpiece of cyberpunk anime. Motoko Kusanagi, the Puppet Master, the ghost-brain question. Kenji Kawai's score. A philosophy lecture with explosions.
Pokémon the anime is a nostalgia trip. Ash and Pikachu travelling around Kanto, Team Rocket's motto, "Who's That Pokémon?" I'd love to see Ash finally win a league. Oh wait, he did.
Naruto is the manga I grew up with. Sasuke leaving the village, Naruto vs. Pain, Kakashi's lightning blade. "Believe it!" I'm 30 and I still cry at Jiraiya's death. #Naruto
One Piece has been running for 27 years and still has me hooked. Luffy's gear 5 reveal was ridiculous. Zoro's getting lost jokes never get old. Oda is a legend. Wano arc still the best.
Berserk is bleak, brilliant and hard to recommend. Guts's story, the Eclipse, the Band of the Hawk. Miura's art is unmatched. RIP Kentaro Miura. Still waiting for the ending we'll never get.
JJK's Shibuya Incident arc is incredible. Gojo being sealed shocked the whole fandom, and Sukuna vs. Mahoraga was cinematic. Gege Akutami can write a mean fight scene.
Haikyu!! made me a volleyball fan. Hinata and Kageyama's freak duo, Karasuno's dream of nationals. The final match with Inarizaki had me up until 3am. Flying!
Vinland Saga starts as a revenge story and becomes a story about peace. Thorfinn's growth is incredible. The slave arc on Ketil's farm was a slow burn that paid off. "I have no enemies."
Dandadan is a hilarious mix of aliens, ghosts and romance. Okarun and Momo's chemistry, Turbo Granny, Evil Eye. Science Saru's anime adaptation is just as good. Yukinobu Tatsu is a genius.
Blue Lock makes football exciting with egos and ruthless selfishness. Isagi, Bachira, Rin Itoshi. The matches are like a battle royale. I've started yelling "I'm the ace striker" in my Sunday league.
Frieren: Beyond Journey's End is a quiet masterpiece. An elf mage reflecting on a ten-year adventure that was a blink to her. Himmel's statues. I cried in the first episode. 🧝
Demon Slayer is Tanjiro's journey to cure his sister, and the visuals in the anime are breathtaking. Nezuko in the box, Zenitsu's thunder breathing. The Entertainment District arc is peak.
Gintama is the funniest manga I've ever read, and then it hits you with the saddest arcs. Gintoki's lazy samurai attitude, Kagura's appetite. Sorachi, you complete lunatic. 🍓
Tokyo Revengers is a time-travel delinquent drama. Takemichi's tears, Mikey's descent, Draken's death scene. It's tragic and addictive. I binged all 31 volumes in a week.
Slam Dunk is the greatest basketball manga ever. Hanamichi Sakuragi, Rukawa, the Shohoku vs. Sannoh match. Takehiko Inoue made me love basketball. "Coach, I'd like to play basketball..." My heart.
Black Clover is an underrated shonen. Asta's "I won't give up!" mantra, the magic knights, Yuno's rivalry. Tabata kept up a weekly pace through 370 chapters. Good vibes.
The Promised Neverland's first arc is the best thriller in manga. The Grace Field escape, Emma, Norman and Ray. The ending's rushed, but the first 37 chapters are perfect.
Watchmen is a once-in-a-generation comic. Rorschach's journal, Doctor Manhattan on Mars, the Comedian's death. Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons made the superhero genre grow up.
Maus is the most important graphic novel ever written. Art Spiegelman tells his father's story of Auschwitz with mice and cats. It's powerful, uncomfortable and necessary. Read it.
Asterix is the comic I grew up with. The magic potion, Obelix's menhirs, the Roman soldiers always getting beaten. "These Romans are crazy!" Goscinny and Uderzo, legends.
Garfield hates Mondays, loves lasagne, and kicks Odie off the table. Jim Davis's strip has run since 1978. Still funny, mostly. "I'm not overweight, I'm undertall."
Persepolis is a moving memoir about growing up in Iran after the revolution. Marjane Satrapi's black-and-white drawings are lovely. Funny, sad, humane. Everyone should read it.
The Sandman is a comic I'll never stop recommending. Neil Gaiman and the artists made something dreamlike and haunting. Morpheus, Death, the Corinthian. Start with Preludes and Nocturnes.
Sin City is stark noir in black and white. Frank Miller's Marv, Hartigan, Nancy. It's brutal, stylised, and not for children. Reading it feels like a cigarette and a bad decision.
The Dark Knight Returns made Batman grim and gritty. Frank Miller's old, angry Bruce Wayne fights Superman in a rain-soaked alley. Fifty years of Bat-history changed with this book.
xkcd is the only comic that teaches me physics, maths and existential dread in the same panel. Randall Munroe is a national treasure. Today's strip about standards was too accurate.

Honestly I should've gone to bed hours ago but I'm in the middle of a Chernobyl rewatch, episode 4 tonight, and the helicopter scene has me gutted. Anyway, I'm also supposed to submit my tax return tomorrow and haven't started. Priorities.

Quick update on my week: finally cleaned out the garage, took the dog to the vet (he's fine, ate a sock), and spent every evening watching Friends reruns because I couldn't bring myself to start anything new. Rachel's wedding dress episode is just so cozy. Will deal with adulthood tomorrow.

My daughter turns 16 on Saturday, and she's having a sleepover with six friends and a long list of snacks. The theme, apparently, is "retro movie night." They want to watch Titanic. I'll be hiding upstairs with a box of tissues, because I know I'll be sobbing at that door scene from the top of the stairs.

We went to the Ghibli exhibition at the museum on Saturday and spent two hours looking at original sketches and cels. My daughter wanted to go straight to the Spirited Away room, and it was gorgeous. The little soot sprites were everywhere. We ended up buying a tiny No-Face keyring for the car.

My cousin has convinced me to finally start One Piece and now I'm 400 chapters in and can't stop. I should be revising for exams. I've been reading on the bus, in the bath, and under the desk. Luffy is a better role model than my uni lecturer. Sorry, Mum.

THREAD on what we actually know about the Gaza hospital strike, because the first 24 hours of reporting were a mess.

1/ Early casualty figures came from the health ministry and were not independently verified.
2/ Satellite imagery published by two different outlets shows damage to the northern wing, but not the full compound.
3/ The IDF and Hamas blamed each other within the hour. Neither claim had been verified by anyone outside the conflict at that point.
4/ Reuters, AP and the BBC have since added caveats to their earlier headlines. Worth reading the corrections, not just the first story.
5/ The honest answer in the first day is "we don't know yet", and that is a perfectly respectable thing for a newsroom to say.

Long read from the Guardian on the Siberian permafrost thaw, and it is genuinely alarming. Whole villages in Yakutia are sinking, roads buckle every spring, and in places they're finding old methane pockets that just blow out of the ground, leaving craters you can see from space. Scientists quoted say the carbon feedback is probably underestimated in most climate models. Not clickbait, not doom for the sake of it. Why is nobody talking about the water crisis in Mexico City? Reservoirs are at record lows, entire neighbourhoods go weeks without taps, and the trucks that deliver water are charging more than a month's rent in some places. It's the same pattern we saw in Cape Town, and if you read the hydrology reports the city is sinking about 20 cm a year because of aquifer drawdown. This is going to be one of the defining stories of the decade and it barely makes the evening news.

I volunteer with a local newsroom and I want to say something about the "fake news" posts I keep seeing. Most errors I deal with aren't lies, they're rushed copy and a source that changed their story. When we get it wrong we publish a correction at the top, we don't quietly delete. If your outlet of choice doesn't do that, ask why. And if you see a screenshot of a headline, find the actual article before you quote-tweet. It takes two minutes. #medialiteracy

Nothing prepares you for the quiet of the Sahara at night. We left the camp at 2am, walked up a dune, and just sat there. No light, no wind, so many stars it felt fake. I'm still thinking about it three weeks later.

Climbed to the summit of Kilimanjaro on day 6 at sunrise. Altitude was brutal, and I cried a bit at the top, but the guides made it feel like a family trip. Total cost: about $2,400 for the week. Plan 8 days if you can, it helps with acclimatisation.

Holiday booking tip: if your flight's cancelled, ask the airline for a refund, not a voucher. Know the rules for your country. In the EU you may be owed up to €600 in compensation, depending on the distance. Keep every receipt.

Anyone been to Palestine recently? Looking for tips on visiting Bethlehem, Hebron and Ramallah responsibly, ideally with local guides. I want to spend money where it helps and learn from people who live there.
Quick one: what's the best way to get from Heathrow to central London at 11pm? Tube's closed, Uber is £70, and I have a toddler. The N9 night bus takes forever. Looking for sanity-saving suggestions.

If you're visiting Napoleon's tomb in Paris, the Invalides complex is bigger than it looks, so allow three hours. The military museum alone could eat an afternoon. Student tickets are cheaper than the website suggests if you ask at the desk.

The ferry from Piraeus to Santorini is a 5-hour ride that goes through some of the clearest water I've ever seen. We spent half the trip on the top deck, wrapped in blankets, watching islands appear out of the haze.

Spent eight hours at Frankfurt airport on a layover, found a quiet corner, wrote a few postcards, and then chatted to a retired engineer from Ohio about the Apollo missions. He worked on the guidance computer. Best layover ever.

Cruise ship tips: skip the ship's excursions, book local tours at the port, bring your own power strip and lanyard, and always eat breakfast at the buffet but dinner on shore. We saved close to $600 across a week.
Today I finally cleaned the garage. It took 6 hours. I found my high school yearbook and a lot of regret.
Turned 40 today. Feeling surprisingly fine. Birthday dinner then early bed. 🎂
New chapter starts Monday. New job, new city, same overthinking.
Haven't been to the gym in 3 weeks but I did buy new gym shoes, so basically the same thing.
My cat just knocked my coffee off the desk and then looked at me like I did it.
Episode 3 of my life: "Man Tries To Assemble Ikea Wardrobe Without Instructions." Spoiler: it's crooked.
Plot twist: I actually enjoyed the group hike. Never thought I'd say that.
Therapy has been the best money I've ever spent. That's it. That's the post.
Day 12 of not checking my phone before breakfast. Feeling lighter. Also bored. Mostly lighter.

My therapist asked me what I do for fun and I couldn't answer. Not one thing. That's a plot twist I wasn't ready for. So I signed up for a pottery class. Tuesday evenings. Wish me luck. I'll probably make a lot of bowls that look like hats.

It's weird how a small thing, like a stranger holding a door open or a barista remembering your name, can completely change the mood of a day. Today I was having a rough one, and an old man at the bus stop told me my scarf was nice. I smiled for an hour.

Spent my entire Saturday lost in a deep clean of the flat and found three socks I thought were gone forever, a missing earring, a 2019 receipt for Nike trainers, and my dog's favourite ball under the sofa. Worth every minute. Felt like an archaeological dig.

Told my boss today that I need to leave at 5pm on Thursdays for my evening class and he just said "of course." I spent two weeks agonising over it. Lesson learned: ask for the thing. Most of the time the answer is fine.
Day 100 of learning the cello. My neighbours have not complained yet. My sound has progressed from "angry goose" to "slightly sad goose." Progress! Anyone who has tips for bow control, I'm listening.

Tried to explain my job to my grandmother for 40 minutes. At the end she said "so you sit at a computer." Yes, Nana. I sit at a computer. She was completely right and also completely missing the point.

Spent the whole evening at my sister's housewarming. Nine adults, four dogs, and one lone cactus that survived the move. The talk was about dentists, mortgage rates, and whether the neighbour's fence is on the property line. This is adulthood and I'm weirdly content.
Selena from the front desk brought homemade tamales for the whole floor today and I think I'm in love. Everyone's mood improved by 40%. She refuses to share the recipe and I respect that.

Got a letter in the post from an old friend I haven't spoken to in 11 years. A real, handwritten, stamped letter. I read it twice and sat on the stairs for ten minutes. We're meeting for coffee on Friday.
Is it normal to feel nostalgic for a time that was actually quite hard? I look at pictures from my first flat and I miss it, even though I had no heating and a mouse called Gerald. Memory is strange.
I find it funny that my entire personality at work is "the person who always has a spare charger." Honestly it's a good brand.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid. Let that sink in.
The Titanic ship carried lifeboats for about half the passengers. Rules at the time were based on tonnage, not people.
Lincoln gave the Gettysburg Address in about two minutes. Everyone else spoke for hours. Brevity wins.
The Gandhi salt march was 240 miles on foot. It changed a movement.
Gorbachev died in 2022, and the reactions in Russia and abroad couldn't have been more different.
Picasso's Guernica was painted in a matter of weeks after the bombing. Anger is a great motivator.
Churchill's bunker in London is worth a visit. The map room is exactly as they left it in 1945.
The Vikings reached North America around 1000 AD, roughly 500 years before Columbus. L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland is the proof.

Fascinating fact: the Battle of Waterloo lasted a single day, June 18, 1815, but ended 20 years of Napoleonic wars. Rain the night before turned the fields to mud, which delayed the French artillery until late morning. Wellington had the high ground and a reverse slope for cover. Small details change history.

If you've ever wondered where "the whole nine yards" comes from, the answer is that nobody knows. All the neat stories about ammunition belts and cement trucks and kilts are invented later. Linguists have traced the phrase back to the 1900s, but its origin remains a mystery. I find that oddly comforting.

Reading about the Chernobyl liquidators, the 600,000 soldiers, miners and firefighters who cleaned up after the 1986 disaster. Many were told almost nothing about the radiation. The Soviet government's secrecy cost lives, and the cleanup was one of the biggest in history. Their sacrifice needs to be remembered. #Chernobyl

Cleopatra spoke at least nine languages and was the first of her dynasty to learn Egyptian. Think about that for a second: the Ptolemies ruled for 300 years without bothering to learn the language of the people they governed. She changed that. Politically very smart.

On this day in 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon. About 400,000 people worked on the programme. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent about two and a half hours outside, and the whole mission ran on less computing power than your phone. Still a staggering achievement.

Gandhi and Tagore disagreed on many things, including how to respond to the colonial system, whether the spinning wheel was a political tool, and what education should be. That friendly disagreement between two giants of the era is one of the great intellectual conversations of the 20th century.

Oppenheimer's security hearing in 1954 was less a trial than a character assassination. The records are public now, and you can see how the AEC board treated him, with testimony from old colleagues like Teller that left a bitter legacy in the physics community.

Fun fact: the Roman Empire didn't fall in a single day in 476 AD. Contemporary writers barely noticed. The eastern half carried on for another thousand years as Byzantium. The notion of a dramatic ending is mostly a later tidy-up by historians who like neat chapters.

The first modern Olympic Games in Athens in 1896 had 14 countries and about 240 athletes. The marathon was invented for them to commemorate the legendary run from Marathon to Athens. A Greek shepherd named Spyridon Louis won, and the crowd went wild.

Lennon and Dylan had a famous late-night meeting in a New York hotel in 1964, where Dylan introduced the Beatles to cannabis. That one evening reportedly shaped the next two albums. History's great collaborations are often just two people in a room.

Lagos was a small Portuguese trading post before the British took it in 1861. Today it's one of the largest cities in Africa. Walk any street and you can see the layers: colonial architecture, mid-century offices, and a skyline full of cranes.

The French Revolution began with a financial crisis, not a philosophical one. The treasury was empty, bread prices were up, and a poor harvest the year before turned a political dispute into a mass uprising. Philosophy gave it a vocabulary, but hunger gave it a crowd.
Gravity is the weakest of the four fundamental forces by a ridiculous margin. A fridge magnet beats the entire Earth.
The Apollo samples are still being analysed in new ways, 50 years later. Never throw away your data.
Fun fact: a day on Venus is longer than its year. Sort of. 🪐
Venom from some snakes is being studied as a source of new blood-pressure medication. Nature's pharmacy is wild.
Tesla's actual work on alternating current mattered more than any car company ever will. Fight me.
It takes 8 minutes and 20 seconds for sunlight to reach us. Wave to your ancestors, the light you're seeing left before you finished that sandwich.
Jaws are one of the oldest structures in vertebrate evolution. Without them we'd still be sucking mud like lampreys.

A review of 40 studies on sleep and memory concluded that people who sleep 7-8 hours consistently outperform others on recall tests by up to 20%. Cramming all night doesn't work. Your brain files information while you're asleep, and it files it better when you don't interrupt it. Please go to bed. #science

Oppenheimer is often called the father of the atomic bomb, but the Manhattan Project involved more than 125,000 people. Credit goes to chemists, engineers, mathematicians, even the cooks and drivers. A big project always has a lot of unnamed hands behind the famous name.

Alien life question for the weekend: if microbes exist under the ice of Europa, how would we know? A lander can't drill through 15 km of ice easily, but plumes of vapour shooting out of cracks could be sampled by a passing probe. That's the plan for the Clipper mission. I'm unreasonably excited about it.

How do vaccines work? Short version: they show your immune system a harmless piece of a germ so it learns to recognise the real one. Your body makes antibodies and memory cells. Next time you meet the actual pathogen, your defences respond in hours rather than days. Long version available if anyone's curious.

A neighbour asked me why the sky is blue and I explained Rayleigh scattering for 10 minutes. She asked "so why is it red at sunset?" and I realised I'd lost her in the first sentence. Shorter version: blue light bounces around a lot, so it comes at you from everywhere. At sunset, the light goes through more air and the blue is scattered away.

Ran a small experiment at home with my kids: boiled water in a pan, placed a cold spoon above it, and watched the steam condense. They learned about the water cycle in 5 minutes, and I'm pretty sure it'll stick longer than any worksheet. Hands-on beats slides every time.

Reading a paper on Chernobyl's red forest. Some trees accumulated enough radioactive material that they became a hazard themselves. But parts of the exclusion zone are now full of wolves, lynx and Przewalski's horses, because people left. Nature recovers faster than we expected, even if the isotopes persist. https://example.com/redforest

Neutron stars are the densest objects we can observe without a black hole. A teaspoon of their material would weigh about a billion tonnes. They spin hundreds of times a second and have magnetic fields trillions of times stronger than Earth's. The universe is wild. And that's before you consider how we figured it out from radio blips.

The Large Hadron Collider restarted this week after a three-year upgrade. If you want to feel small, remember that those beams travel at 99.9999991% of the speed of light around a 27 km ring, and the whole thing sits under the French and Swiss border. Particle physics is basically mind-blowing logistics.

If you ever feel unproductive, remember that Darwin spent eight years of his life studying barnacles. Eight. He called himself "a barnacle man." Then he wrote On the Origin of Species. Slow science matters. #AcademicTwitter

Climate scientists have known since the 1970s that burning fossil fuels warms the planet. Exxon's own internal reports predicted the temperature rise accurately. This isn't new knowledge, it's old knowledge that was kept quiet. The question now isn't "do we know?", it's "what are we going to do?"

Elvis the toad (yes, we named him) has been part of our wetlands survey since 2021. We tag each animal with a tiny chip and track where they travel. He's covered 800 metres this season. I never thought I'd get emotional about an amphibian.

Quantum entanglement doesn't let you send messages faster than light. Everybody asks. Two particles can be correlated in a way that defies classical expectation, but you can't use it to carry information on its own. You still need a classical channel. Sorry, sci-fi.
Taylor Swift's Eras Tour at Wembley: 90,000 people singing every word. I cried during the bridge and I'm not sorry. 🎶
John Lennon's Imagine still gets me every single time.
Bob Dylan going electric in 1965 and half the crowd booing is the most rock'n'roll moment ever.
Anyone else listen to the same album on repeat for a week? Currently stuck on Rumours.
The best concert I ever went to was a tiny pub gig with 30 people. No contest.
Saturday night: vinyl, a bottle of wine, and the neighbour's terrible singing next door. Perfect.
Soundcheck at 5, doors at 7, headliner at 9, and my feet are already wrecked. Festival season is here.
Picked up a second-hand guitar for $80 and it sounds better than my old one. Bargains exist!
The live-streaming quality of tonight's Lagos concert was shockingly good. Whole city dancing in my living room. 🇳🇬

There's a particular kind of joy in finding a band you've never heard and realising they have a back catalogue of nine albums. It's like being given a free summer. Just discovered a Brooklyn-based group that sounds like 1970s Laurel Canyon filtered through a drum machine, and I haven't taken the headphones off in two days.

Dylan's Blood on the Tracks is the best breakup album ever recorded, and I'll hear no argument. "Simple Twist of Fate" is perfect. The way the verses shift perspective is what makes it so good: you're never quite sure whose side he's telling from.

Went to see Taylor Swift on the Eras Tour in Vegas last night and the cultural phenomenon is real. A stadium of strangers swapping friendship bracelets, kids on shoulders, grandparents in sequin jackets. Whatever your view of pop, no one can say this wasn't joyful.

Wrote my first song for my daughter's birthday. Three chords, terrible lyrics, a little tune that she asked me to play 14 times. Not planning a record deal. But this is the best thing I've ever created.

Music scene in Lagos is incredible right now. Afrobeats has crossed over everywhere, but the underground is even better: tiny clubs in Surulere, rooftop sessions in Yaba, producers who record on a laptop in a bedroom and end up on every radio in West Africa. If you're ever in town, go out.

Rewatching old live sets from the 1970s and I'm struck by how much space the music breathed. No click track, no autotune, long jams where people just listened to each other. Not saying it's better, just different. Pink Floyd at Pompeii, Allman Brothers at the Fillmore. Real musicians in a room.

My dad started a ukulele group at the care home and they've been rehearsing weekly. Their first public gig is this Friday. Repertoire: Hey Jude, Brown-Eyed Girl, and one very ambitious attempt at a Gershwin medley. Come support them if you're nearby. Free tea.

Concert etiquette thread: don't film the whole show, don't talk through the quiet songs, don't stand in the aisle. The artist can see you. The people behind you are trying to hear. We can all do this. Take one photo and put the phone away.

The Beatles split in 1970, but Lennon and McCartney's final album together came out in 1969. People forget how much happened in the final year. Abbey Road, Let It Be, the rooftop concert... it's a masterclass in how to end a band with dignity, and then argue about it for fifty years.
Kendrick, Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell. Three poets with different tools. If you're not reading lyrics alongside your listening, you're missing half the artistry. Try it on a long train ride.

Anyone know a good local teacher for acoustic guitar in the Bristol area? I'm an adult beginner and I'd like someone patient. Evenings only. No metal, please. My ears and my neighbours have suffered enough.
Snow in Texas?! Again?! The state is not prepared and neither am I.
Storm warning issued for the whole south coast. Stay indoors tonight.
It's 41°C in Dubai and we are all complaining like it's news.
First frost of the year this morning. Time to bring the plants indoors. ❄️
Rain, rain, rain. Day 11. I think my socks are permanently damp.
Alaska today: -22°C, clear sky, aurora forecast strong. Going out with a thermos.
Football season ends and suddenly it's sunny. Coincidence? I think not.
Fog so thick this morning in Rome I couldn't see the end of the street. Atmospheric but terrifying on a scooter.
Heatwave in Siberia. I'll say it again, Siberia. It's not supposed to do this.

Hurricane season is shaping up to be a nasty one. The ocean temperature in the Gulf is 2°C above average, which is basically fuel for storms. If you live on the coast, check your evacuation route now, not when the cone of uncertainty includes your house.

We just had the wettest September on record in my town. 270mm of rain in four weeks, rivers up, fields underwater, the old bridge closed. My tomatoes drowned and so did my patience. At least the ducks are happy.

Flash flood warning in Brooklyn after a stalled thunderstorm dropped 3 inches in an hour. Subway stations flooded, cars stuck, and a delivery guy on an e-bike carried a stranger's dog out of knee-deep water. I love this city.

Weather forecasters have a thankless job. When they're right, nobody notices. When they're wrong by one degree, the whole town complains. Today's forecast said 60% chance of rain and then it rained. Just applaud them. Please.

Today's sunrise over the lake: pink on top, grey beneath, mist rising off the water, one lone fisherman in a rowing boat. No filter. I took forty photos and none of them did it justice. Sometimes you just have to stand there.

Siberia has seen a drop of 40 degrees in 24 hours, and the schoolchildren still go out to play. My Russian friend shrugs when I ask. "It's just weather," he says. "We dress for it." I'm very impressed and slightly jealous of the layers.

Honest question for the weather nerds: why does the first warm day of spring feel warmer than a hotter day in July? Is it contrast? Humidity? The fact I've been in coats for six months? I'm sitting outside in a T-shirt at 14°C and feeling like a lizard.

The Santa Ana winds are back in Los Angeles. Dry air, static in my hair, and fire danger very high. Cal Fire has pre-positioned engines across the foothills. Please be careful with outdoor flames this week. One spark is enough.

If you're stuck in a heatwave: close curtains on the sunny side, open windows at night, drink water, put damp towels on the back of your neck, and check on your older neighbours. It costs nothing and saves lives. Stay cool, friends.

The Easter weekend forecast for Wales is rain, rain, a possible break on Sunday afternoon, and then more rain. Brilliant. I've booked a campsite, a trailer, and a lot of waterproof clothing. We're doing this regardless.

Clear skies, no moon, minimal wind: perfect for the Perseids tonight. I'm lying on a blanket in the garden with a flask and my 8-year-old. 14 meteors so far. She's counting out loud. It's the best night of her summer, and mine.
My boss just scheduled a "quick sync" for 4:45pm on a Friday. Quick. Sync. Sure.
Director of a company, not a film. Just to be clear on my LinkedIn headline. 😂
New quarter, new OKRs, same coffee machine that's been broken since 2022.
Monday meetings should be emails. Emails should be nothing. Nothing should be a walk.
Final interview tomorrow. Please send good vibes and a decent tie. 🙏
Got promoted today! Same desk, same chair, 8% more money. Take the win.
I think the printer knows when I'm in a hurry.
Remote work update: day 4 in a row without putting on real trousers. Productivity at an all-time high.
Whoever keeps microwaving fish in the office kitchen, please reconsider your life choices.

Tips for first-time managers, from someone who made all the mistakes:

1. Don't try to be everyone's friend.
2. Give feedback early, in private, with specifics.
3. Praise in public.
4. Protect your team's focus time.
5. Say "I don't know" when you don't.
6. Take your holiday.
Your team watches what you do, not what you say.

Job hunting at 45 is brutal. Applications ignored, "overqualified" feedback, and recruiters who are younger than my first car. But last week I got an interview for a role I'd actually love, so I'm choosing to be hopeful. If you hear of any operations roles in Manchester, I'm all ears.

A shout-out to the cleaners at our office, who arrive at 5am and leave before most of us wake. They've been in the building eleven years and know everyone's names. We left a card and a gift basket for them at the front desk. Thank the people who make your workplace work.

Interviewing for a senior role this week. The panel includes the director of operations, two team leads, and someone from HR. I've done my homework: their last three press releases, the CEO's recent podcast, and the Glassdoor reviews. Will report back. Fingers crossed. 🤞

Our CEO announced that "culture is our competitive advantage" at the all-hands, then cut the budget for the annual team retreat, the learning stipend, and the coffee. Culture is what people do when the budget's gone, apparently.

Wrote a letter of resignation, tore it up, wrote another, put it in a drawer, took it out, rewrote it, and finally sent it. It took me three weeks. I feel lighter. Whatever's next, I'll figure it out.

Why do "urgent" requests always arrive at 4:55pm on Friday? Why. Every time. I've started leaving at 4:30 to dodge the whole thing, and my boss has noticed but hasn't said a word. Maybe she's doing the same.

Our client meeting ran 3 hours, produced 4 action items, and the best idea of the day came from the intern during the coffee break. Never underestimate the person who isn't afraid to ask the obvious question.
Reminder that it's okay to say no to a task you don't have time for. Say it clearly, offer an alternative, and don't over-explain. The people who respect you will respect you more.
Boss: "Can we do a 15-minute call?" Me: "Sure." The call: 1 hour 40 minutes. The conclusion: "Let's follow up next week."
Mortgage rates dropped 0.25% this week. Cautiously optimistic. 🏠
Opened a Roth IRA today. Better late than never.
Bitcoin's volatile again. I'm not touching it. Index funds and chill.
My electricity bill doubled and I did not double my usage. Explain.
Spent $14 on a sandwich and $6 on a coffee today. Inflation or lack of self-control? Both.
Tesla stock is up 6% on no news. Markets are vibes now.
Amazon's earnings beat expectations again, and its cloud division is the star. Boring but steady.
The best investment I made this year was a good pair of shoes. Ten miles a day and zero regrets.
If your emergency fund is less than three months of expenses, start there. Boring, effective, life-changing.

We finally paid off the last of our student loans after 11 years. A small party in the kitchen: two glasses of sparkling water and a cheap cake. The weight that came off my shoulders is hard to describe. If you're in the middle of it, keep going.

Hear me out: budgeting isn't about restricting yourself, it's about knowing where the money goes. I use a simple spreadsheet with five categories and one rule, which is that anything over $100 gets a 48-hour wait. My impulse buying dropped by about 70%.

Interest rates have an effect on every part of daily life: mortgages, car loans, credit cards, savings. When the Bank of England raised rates again, my monthly payment went up £210. For some of my friends it was twice that. The ripple through households is real, and nobody's talking about it enough.

I'm 28 and I don't understand pensions, so I spent a weekend reading about them. Short version: start early, contribute at least enough to get the employer match, pick a low-cost fund, ignore the noise. Don't let the jargon scare you away. It really does boil down to that.

Small business owner here. Cash flow is the thing that kills you, not profit. You can be profitable on paper and still miss payroll if clients pay in 90 days. Invoice quickly, chase politely, and keep two months of costs in the bank. Learn from my near-disaster in 2019.

Bought my first house at 36. It took eight years of saving, two jobs, and a lot of cheap pasta. We got the keys on a Friday, sat on the floor of the empty living room and ate fish and chips. Best meal of my life. Home isn't just a word, it's a place you can finally paint.

Why do airlines charge $60 to pick a seat? The base fare has become a teaser. You end up paying twice the price after adding bags, meals and seats. Read the total cost before you click confirm. It saved me about $200 on my last trip.

Everyone loves a side hustle story, but mine is boring. I fix bicycles on Saturdays in my garage. I make about $400 a month, keep the receipts, and put it in an index fund. In ten years it'll be worth about $60,000. Nothing glamorous, just compound interest doing its job.

My accountant told me to keep every receipt for seven years. I now have a box of paper receipts that could fill a small boat. Digital scanning is my next project. Hopefully the tax authority likes PDFs.

Retirement isn't a number, it's a lifestyle. Spend a year tracking exactly what you spend, then ask yourself how much of it you'd miss. For most people it's far less than the scare-mongering figures online.

Thinking about switching banks after the app locked me out for three days. Customer service said "try again in 24 hours." Twice. I can't be the only one. Anyone recommend a decent credit union in Ohio?
Drinking more water has done more for my headaches than any pill.
Flu season is early this year. Get the shot, wash your hands, stay home if you're sick.
Doctor said "you're fine, just tired." I'm fine, just tired. That's the whole diagnosis.
Day 30 of no sugar. I've seen things. I've done things. I want a biscuit.
My physio told me to stop sitting like a question mark. I'm trying.
Had a really bad episode of vertigo this morning. The doctor says it's inner ear. Please don't laugh at my walking.
Broke my arm skiing. The cast is bright blue. The kids want to sign it. This is not a victory.
Back at the gym after a month off. My legs feel like they belong to a stranger.
Mental health isn't a trend, it's a condition. Be kind.

Thread on sleep hygiene that actually worked for me.

- Fixed bedtime and wake-up time, even on weekends
- No screens after 10pm
- Bedroom at 18°C
- Caffeine only before noon
- Magnesium before bed (checked with my GP first)
Took about three weeks to feel the difference. Now I wake up before my alarm.

Just got my blood test results back and my vitamin D is on the floor. The doctor asked about my diet, my sun exposure, my sleep, and then said "winter in the UK, it's a classic." Prescription is 2000IU a day and a walk at lunchtime. Easy fix, apparently.

Long COVID is not "just being tired." Three years on, I still lose words mid-sentence, my heart races walking up stairs, and I need naps that last two hours. I used to run marathons. Please, if someone tells you they're struggling with it, believe them.

Started physiotherapy for my knee after a football injury. The therapist said, "Rehab is boring on purpose." Three sets of ten, five days a week, for eight weeks. I'm on week five and I can already walk downstairs without wincing. Slow progress is still progress.

If you wear contact lenses, never sleep in them or rinse them with tap water. I ended up with an eye infection last month that cost me four days off work and a very scary look at an ophthalmologist's light. It's a small habit with large consequences.

My six-year-old's first dentist visit was a triumph. She sat in the big chair, held up a mirror, and informed the dentist that "teeth are for biting, not brushing." The dentist laughed and gave her a sticker. Zero cavities. Parenting win.

Spent my weekend on a silent meditation retreat, no phones, no talking, no books. By day two I was bored; by day three I was crying for no reason; by day four I felt calm in a way I'd forgotten. Not for everyone, but I'd go again. Highly recommend for burnt-out overthinkers.

One Saturday I decided to walk 10,000 steps, and by Wednesday I was doing 12,000 without noticing. Weight is down slightly, mood is up significantly. No gadgets except a cheap pedometer. Walking is underrated.
Does anyone have tips for a nasty cough that won't go away? Third week now. I've tried honey, steam, rest. GP says it's post-viral and could last six weeks. Please send me lemon tea and patience.

Hospital visits are exhausting even when you aren't the patient. Sat with Mum for eight hours yesterday, did the crossword, watched people come and go, and the nurses were remarkable. Thank you to everyone in the NHS. You are doing a hard job under hard conditions.
My 4-year-old just told the neighbour that Daddy "works at a computer and hates Mondays." Accurate.
Our family WhatsApp group has 47 unread messages and all of them are about who's bringing the potato salad.
Mum turned 70 today and insisted on doing her own cake. It's lopsided and perfect. 🎂
My son's first word was "dog." Not mama. Not dada. Dog. We've accepted it.
Grandpa's famous pancakes, Sunday morning, no phones. Life's good.
Spent the afternoon teaching my daughter to ride a bike. We both have scraped knees. Zero regrets.
Our elderly cat and our newborn have reached a peace treaty. Mostly she just ignores him. He adores her.
Thanksgiving prep: three pies, one turkey, one very opinionated aunt. Send help.
Dad's retirement party was last night. He gave a speech and the whole room cried. Even the caterers.

We have a family rule that on the first Sunday of every month, everyone cooks one dish from a country none of us have visited. Last month was Peru. This month's Ethiopia. My teenager complained for exactly four minutes, then asked for seconds, then asked when we're doing the next one. The kitchen's a mess and I'm quietly delighted.

Our family tradition is to spend Christmas Eve at my grandmother's flat in Brooklyn, where 22 people squeeze into a living room built for six. We sit on the floor, on the radiator, on each other. She makes enough food for 50. She is 91, and still won't let anyone else do the gravy. Some traditions deserve to last forever.

Telling my toddler "no" is like talking to a very small, very determined lawyer. She argues every point, offers three alternatives, and then pretends not to hear. We had a twenty-minute negotiation about socks this morning. I lost.

Raising teenagers is a lot like running a small hotel where the guests never tip and complain about the Wi-Fi. But then one of them hugs you at the school gate, in front of their friends, and you remember why you do it. I'll take that hug over any five-star review.

My parents have been married for 52 years and their secret, according to my mother, is separate bathrooms and a short memory. My father says it's "yes, dear." They both laugh at each other's answers. I hope for half of what they have.

Dear parents of newborns: it gets easier. The first six weeks are a blur of feeds and tears (yours and theirs), but around month three something shifts. You start sleeping in longer stretches, you start laughing again, and one day your baby smiles at you on purpose. I promise it's worth it.

A letter from my grandfather, written in 1962, arrived in a box of old photos. He wrote about the harvest, the price of wheat, my grandmother's new dress, and that he was "worried about the cold snap." Eighty years of weather and worry between us and not much has changed. I framed it.

We've started a family podcast, just for ourselves: the kids interview Grandma about her childhood. She told us about leaving Poland in 1968, her first job in a bakery, and the day she met Grandpa. Seven episodes so far. Nobody else will ever hear them. We'll treasure them forever.
Got my son's school report and the teacher wrote "a delightful young man with a very loud voice." Both are true, and the second is truer in the car.

Watching my dad teach my son how to fish at the lake this morning, three generations on one dock, no phones, just the water and a very tangled line. I love moments like this more than I can say. #family
Pothole on Elm Street has now been there longer than my marriage.
Farmers market opens Saturday at 8. Come early for the good tomatoes.
Library is hosting a free coding class for kids on Wednesdays. Details at the front desk.
Anyone know why the traffic lights on Main and 5th have been flashing red for two days?
Our local bakery just won a regional award. So proud of this little shop. 🥖
Lost cat, orange tabby, answers to Biscuit. Last seen near the park on Maple. Please DM if you see him. 🙏
Town council meeting Thursday, 7pm, to vote on the new bike lanes. Show up if you care.
Congrats to the Eastside Under-12s for their first win of the season. Hot chocolate on me!
The old bus depot downtown is being turned into a community centre. Finally.

The bus route 42 has been cut back to every hour and it's a lifeline for half the elderly in our area. The council claims it's a temporary measure, but it's been "temporary" for 14 months. Sign the petition here and write to your councillor. https://example.com/petition

The new roundabout on Station Road has been open for a week and I've now watched four drivers go the wrong way. A series of confused faces, one honked horn and a delivery van that did a full 360. Local drivers, we can do better.

Our school's PTA is running a fundraiser to put a new roof on the music room. We're about 60% of the way there. A raffle, a bake sale and a talent show on 14 March. Come along. It's a fun evening and it's all for the kids. Tickets at the door, £5 including tea.

There's a new pop-up food market on the high street every Friday evening and it's brilliant. Falafel, Jamaican patties, Polish doughnuts. A whole crowd of neighbours sitting on the kerb with paper plates, chatting. This is how a town should feel on a weekend.

Brooklyn Public Library's summer reading challenge is back. If you're a parent: sign your kid up. Prizes, events, and an excuse to explore the branch you've been meaning to try. Our local branch is running a puppet show on Saturday that's honestly better than most adult plays.

Missing: a green parrot named Gus, escaped from a window on Birch Lane yesterday afternoon. Very chatty, will say "hello gorgeous" in a Yorkshire accent. If you hear a parrot flirting in your hedge, please call. Reward: unlimited gratitude and a cake.
The Palestine Solidarity group at the community hall meets on Thursdays at 6:30. Open to everyone, free tea, no pressure. Talks, letter-writing, and sometimes cake. Just turn up. #Palestine

The pond behind the church was drained last week, and the volunteers found 14 shopping trolleys, 3 bicycles, and one very surprised old frog. The pond's being refilled now, and a planting day is scheduled for next weekend. Please help us make it beautiful.

Our neighbourhood's volunteer fire brigade is celebrating 100 years this weekend. Open day at the station, kids can sit in the fire engine, and there's a barbecue and a raffle. Thank you to everyone who has served over the decades.

Taxi drivers in my town just got a new fare structure that nobody told them about. A friend drives a cab in Lagos and says every city has the same problem: the people who make the rules never ride in the vehicles. Local government needs to try the job first.
Spotted a kingfisher on the river this morning. Blue flash, gone in a second. Made my week. 🐦
Alaska's glaciers are retreating faster than any model predicted. Worth seeing before it's too late.
First bluebells of the year in the woods today. Spring is officially here.
My Venus flytrap ate its first fly this week and I felt like a proud parent.
Saw two foxes playing in the garden at dawn. They had no idea I was watching.
The whale watching trip from Reykjavik was unreal. Humpbacks breaching 50 metres away. 🐋
Vikings buried their dead at this beach, apparently. I'm in Norway and the fjord is silent. Just beautiful.
Cleared the garden plot this weekend. Found three snails, a toad and what I'm fairly sure was a lost marble.
Rocky coastline, high tide, one flask of tea. Nature's therapy session.

Went out at dawn to count the birds at our local reserve. Forty-two species, including a first sighting of a marsh harrier. Not bad for two hours before breakfast. The volunteers do this every year, and the data goes to the national survey. Join if you're curious, no experience needed, just binoculars and patience.

The sand dunes at Lençóis Maranhenses in Brazil flood every rainy season, filling with turquoise lagoons that look unreal. Fish appear out of nowhere. I'd read about it, but nothing prepared me for the walk across the dunes at sunset, barefoot, the sand still warm and the pools perfectly still.

It's the sixth year of my wildlife garden and I finally have a hedgehog family. I left a pile of logs in the corner, a shallow dish of water and no slug pellets. They arrived within a season. Do not underestimate how little nature needs from us. Mostly it needs us to stop tidying.

Alaska is bigger than it looks on maps, and it looks pretty big on maps. We drove for six days and hit three national parks, two glaciers and one very confused moose in the middle of the road. The silence is the best part, a quiet you can almost lean on.

My grandfather planted an oak when my father was born, and my father planted one when I was born. This week I planted one when my daughter was born. Three oaks, three generations, one hillside. It's the best family tradition we have. Plant something that will outlive you.

If you see a lost fledgling on the ground, leave it alone. Its parents are usually nearby and still feeding it. Moving it can do more harm than good. Only intervene if it's injured or in danger. I volunteer for a wildlife rescue and we get far too many "orphans" that weren't orphans at all.

Siberian tigers are making a slow comeback in the Russian Far East thanks to anti-poaching patrols, camera traps and a lot of unglamorous fieldwork. The population has grown from around 40 in the 1930s to over 500 today. Conservation works when people commit to it. A rare good-news story. https://example.com/tigers

The Amazon at dawn, rowing a narrow boat through flooded forest while pink river dolphins surfaced beside us. The guide killed the engine, and we all went quiet. A howler monkey started up somewhere far off, and the whole canopy answered. I'll remember it until I die.

Beautiful weekend in the Lake District. A long walk, a pub with a log fire, and a sheepdog that adopted our group for the day. He walked beside us for six miles, then trotted off at the car park like he'd finished a shift.

Just heard the first cuckoo of the year in my village. April 11. My neighbour has recorded it every spring since 1994 in a little notebook. The dates are creeping earlier. Citizen science is a quiet kind of heroism.

Been following the Gaza ceasefire negotiations all week and I think the most useful thing I can do is point you to primary sources instead of opinions. The UN OCHA situation reports are public and updated daily, the Israeli and Palestinian statements are on their ministries' official pages, and Reuters and AP have pooled wire copy that's careful about attribution. Start there, then read the commentary. #Gaza #Israel #Palestine https://example.com/ocha

It has been 40 years since the Chernobyl disaster and the story is still being rewritten. The new containment arch over the reactor is holding, but a drone strike dented the roof last year and engineers are worried about repair costs. Meanwhile the town of Slavutych, built for evacuated workers, is still home to thousands. The anniversary coverage in Kyiv this week was sober and good. If you only know the old headlines, look at the new ones.

Spent the morning at the vigil outside the embassy in Berlin. Several hundred people, mostly quiet, many holding candles, some with signs naming their relatives in Ukraine. A woman next to me told me her sister's flat in Odesa had been hit twice in a month. A teenager played the cello. A volunteer handed out tea in paper cups. No speeches, just people standing together in the cold. It was the most human thing I've seen in weeks.

The Lagos state government has announced a new flood-warning system, with sirens and SMS alerts for low-lying districts like Ajegunle and Makoko. I'm cautiously optimistic: the old system existed on paper and never really worked. The test sirens last weekend were audible across the lagoon, and people I spoke to knew what to do. Now they need to maintain the drains. @LagosStateGovt #Lagos https://example.com/lagos-alerts

If you want a sensible way to read the news without losing your mind: pick two outlets from different parts of the political spectrum, read the news section, skip the comments, and check the date on every story. A shocking-sounding headline from 2019 gets recirculated all the time. I've seen friends angry about a flood in Texas that happened six years ago. A minute of checking saves a lot of anger. #medialiteracy

Dubai's real-estate boom keeps making headlines, and I'm not sure what to make of it. Tower after tower, record prices, and a wave of new residents from Europe, India, and Russia. The skyline outside my window has changed three times in four years. I work in logistics, and I can tell you the cranes are not slowing down, but nor are the living costs. Everyone I know is renting and wondering how long it lasts.

A short thread on Alaska's wildfire season in 2025, as someone who lives in Fairbanks. The smoke has been so thick some mornings that school buses ran with headlights on at 9am. Our hospital saw a 30% jump in respiratory visits. Crews are exhausted, camped out in tents, rotating every 14 days. The state asked for out-of-state help twice. People talk about climate as an abstraction. Here, it's the air you breathe.

I attended the town hall for our congressman last night and, to give him credit, he took 90 minutes of hostile questions without losing his temper. The topics: healthcare costs, the border, Ukraine funding, a proposed highway through the old orchard. Nobody got a straight answer on the highway. But people came, argued, and left in one piece. That's something. Local democracy is boring, tiring, and necessary. #localpolitics

The thing about Gorbachev that gets lost in the Cold War stories is how limited his options actually were. He inherited an economy in free fall, a party apparatus that resisted any change, and a population that wanted both reform and stability. Glasnost let out decades of pent-up anger. His mistake, or his greatness, was believing the system could be reformed rather than replaced. Historians still argue about it. I find the argument more interesting than the verdict.

People are pretending the debate about Palestine and Israel is just two sides screaming, but the actual policy questions are boringly specific: the status of Jerusalem, borders, refugees, settlements, security guarantees. Each one has a decades-long paper trail. If you want to have a useful conversation, read the Oslo accords, read the Arab Peace Initiative, read the Geneva proposals. Then argue. Honestly it's the only way to stop the shouting. #Palestine #Israel

Texas has just passed another voting law and, without taking a side on the substance, I wish politicians would stop describing it in the most extreme terms possible. Read the bill. It's 40 pages. It changes ID requirements, drop-box rules, and early voting hours. You can think those are good or bad, but you can't claim it's either the end of democracy or the salvation of it. #Election2024

Honestly, the filibuster debate is like watching two people argue about the offside rule. Everyone's passionate, nobody has read the rulebook, and the actual outcome depends on a technical point that most people don't understand. Here's a one-minute explanation: a filibuster blocks a vote by extending debate, and it takes 60 senators to end it. That's all. That's the whole drama. Now go vote in your primary.

Reading Lincoln's second inaugural address again and the line that gets me is "with malice toward none, with charity for all." It was delivered six weeks before he died, to a country exhausted by four years of war. Today we can't manage charity in a comment section. We've lost something and I'm not sure how to get it back, but I'd like to try.

To the people complaining about the "tone" of political ads: yes, they've always been brutal. Look at the 1800 campaign between Jefferson and Adams. One side called the other a hermaphroditical character; the other side said Jefferson would bring civil war and open prostitution. We've been hating each other in print for 225 years. It's not new, only faster.

Reading through Proverbs this month, one chapter a day, since there are 31 chapters. It's a brilliant way to do it. Today's was chapter 15, which opens with "A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger." I read that in the morning and then, at 8:15, had a tense email thread with a colleague. I wrote a gentle reply. The whole thing ended in two lines. The old book has a point. #Proverbs #bible
